segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Then the kingdom of the heavens will be like ten young women who took their torches and went out to meet the bridegroom.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Five of them were foolish and five were sensible.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For when the foolish ones took their torches, they took no oil with them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but the sensible ones took oil in flasks along with their torches.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But in the middle of the night there was a shout: ‘Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then all those young women got up and got their torches ready.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The foolish ones said to the sensible, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our torches are going out.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the sensible ones answered, ‘No, there would never be enough for us and for you. Go instead to the dealers and buy some for yourselves.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But while they were going off to buy it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Later the other young women came too, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open up for us!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But he answered, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So stay awake, because you do not know the day or the hour.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “For it is like a man about to go abroad, who called his own slaves and handed over his property to them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one—to each according to his own ability—and he went abroad. At once

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: the one who had received the five talents went and put them to work and gained five more.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In the same way the one with the two gained two more.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But the one who had received the one went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: After a long time the master of those slaves came and settled accounts with them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one who had received the five talents came forward and brought five more talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over five talents to me. See, I have gained five more talents.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few things; I will put you in charge of many. Enter into the joy of your master.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one with the two talents also came forward and said, ‘Master, you handed over two talents to me. See, I have gained two more talents.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave! You were faithful over a few things; I will put you in charge of many. Enter into the joy of your master.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then the one who had received the one talent also came forward and said, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So I was afraid, and I went off and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what is yours.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But his master answered him, ‘You wicked and lazy slave! You knew, did you, that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and when I came I would have received back what was mine with interest.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So take the talent away from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have more than enough; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And throw the worthless slave out into the outer darkness. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate people from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and he will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then the king will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me a drink, I was a stranger and you took me in,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did it for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did it for me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then he will also say to those on his left, ‘Go away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me no drink,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I was a stranger and you did not take me in, naked and you did not clothe me, sick and in prison and you did not look after me.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then they too will answer, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve you?’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then he will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it for one of the least of these, you did not do it for me either.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

notes.note: Matthew's Greek has the plural, “heavens,” a Semitic turn of phrase that a first-century hearer would have noticed. Most English translations flatten it to “heaven”; the plural is kept here wherever the Greek has it.

The Greek word denotes an unmarried girl of marriageable age, who was assumed to be a virgin. Most versions have “virgins” and some “bridesmaids.” In this story the point is the girls' role as young unmarried attendants at the wedding, and “virgins” puts the emphasis in the wrong place for a modern reader. “Bridesmaids” was not chosen because it suggests a modern wedding custom.

The usual meaning of this word is “torch” (as in John 18:3); the ordinary word for a household oil lamp is a different one. Many commentators picture sticks wrapped in oil-soaked rags, carried in a night-time wedding procession, which burn briefly and must be re-soaked from a flask. The word can also mean “lamp,” and most translations and some lexicons take it that way here, so the traditional rendering remains possible.
The Greek word describes practical good sense and foresight, and is different from the usual word for “wise.” Most translations have “wise” here; “prudent” would also be accurate.

The Greek word means a person owned by a master, not a hired employee. Most English versions soften it to “servants,” though some use “slaves.” Slaves in the ancient world could be given great financial responsibility, as here.

This is the ordinary Greek verb for transferring something into another's control, and it is rendered “hand over” throughout this translation so that the reader can see where the same word recurs. Most versions have “entrusted” or “delivered” here, which is the same sense.

A talent was a weight of silver or gold and the largest unit of money in use, worth about six thousand denarii, or roughly twenty years' wages for a day laborer. Even the slave given one talent is handed a very large sum. The English use of “talent” for a natural ability derives from this parable; in the story itself the word means only money.

One Greek word serves both for “nations” and, in the plural, for “Gentiles,” the non-Jewish peoples. Most interpreters take the phrase here to mean all humanity, as in 24:14 and 28:19, and the translation follows them. Some hold that it means the Gentiles specifically, judged by how they treated Jesus' followers.

The verb means going to see someone out of concern for their welfare, and with the sick as object it implies practical care. Most versions keep “visited,” which in modern English suggests no more than a social call. Some versions already have “looked after” or “took care of.”

The Greek plural “brothers” regularly includes women. Who is meant is disputed. Elsewhere in Matthew, Jesus' “brothers” are his disciples (12:49–50; 28:10), and many scholars take the phrase here to mean his followers or his messengers. Others take it to mean anyone in need. The Greek does not settle the question.

The same Greek adjective describes the fire here and both the punishment and the life in verse 46. It is related to the word for “age,” and in Jewish usage it often describes what belongs to the age to come, so it is a matter of kind as well as length. “Eternal” is the standard rendering; a minority of translators prefer “of the age to come.”

candidates.reason: Occurs throughout the New Testament in parables and as a self-designation of apostles; translators divide between “slave,” “servant” and “bondservant,” and variation would hide a single Greek word.
The choice between “virgin,” “young woman,” “girl” and “bridesmaid” affects Matthew 1:23, Luke 1:27, 1 Corinthians 7 and Revelation 14:4, and needs one policy by sense.
Recurs in Matthew 7:24, 10:16, 24:45, in Luke and in Paul; translators vary between “wise,” “prudent,” “sensible” and “shrewd,” and it should be kept distinct from σοφός.
Recurs in the watchfulness sayings, Gethsemane, Paul and Revelation; “watch,” “keep watch,” “stay awake” and “be alert” are all in use, and the link between passages is lost if it varies.
The plural used of mixed groups appears in nearly every book; whether to render “brothers,” “brothers and sisters” or “fellow believers” needs one policy.

findings.greek: Μήποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν
findings.english: No, there would never be enough for us and for you
findings.problem: Μήποτε expresses apprehension ('perhaps there will not be enough'). 'Would never be enough' turns a cautious concern into a flat, absolute certainty.
